cron.description: 6-field Quartz cron of the menu tick (MENU_CRON). Cron runs in UTC. It is a TICK and not a birth because the substrate hands a cell no message at spawn: the first ask is the first tick, and every later one is how a tool ADDED to the tools hive by mutation reaches this agent at all.

description.purpose: The tick that makes this collector ASK the tools hive for the declarations of the tools its agent uses (GH #464). It sends, it decides nothing: WHICH names are asked for is ./assemble's `params.tools`, and whether anything is asked at all is that list being non-empty.
description.use_when: Inside the collector hive. Retune the cadence with MENU_CRON, or per instance with add/modify/remove ops by schedule_id; `trigger` re-asks now, without waiting for the cron.
description.not_in_scope: No catch-up, no knowledge of tools, and NOTHING to do with the two schedules this hive deliberately does not have. The prune lane and the stale-round exit stay operator-driven and arithmetic (`collector/README.md`): both would DESTROY or CLOSE state, and a template that fired those itself would be deciding when somebody's turns fall. A menu tick creates nothing and destroys nothing -- it asks a question whose answer overwrites one slot with the same value until something over there changes. And no uuid7 TOKEN in the schedule id, which every other shipped timer carries: that token is an INSTANTIATION substitution with no filesystem-side producer, so a tree written straight to disk -- which is how this hive is read all over the test corpus and how a hand-built colony is written -- refuses to BOOT on it (`unsupported_substitution`). A timer's key space is its own `cell.db` and this template ships exactly one schedule, so the label buys nothing a constant does not, and the constant costs no boot.
description.emits_meaning: A plain trigger. The edge out of this cell names the lane; the body is empty because the request is assembled where the declaration lives.
description.consumes_meaning: Schedule ops (add/modify/remove/trigger by schedule_id) as body.op.
examples: every five minutes -> ./assemble on in_menu_tick; a collector with no declared tools answers with silence
{"op": "trigger", "schedule_id": "..."} -> the menu is re-asked at once, after a tool was added to the hive
